coverage.summary: Authored three worked examples covering all distinct retained assessment methods, using supplied booklet methods and changed values. Practice and quiz mathematics were neither altered nor re-audited. Questions and solutions are separate; solution prose remains editable and inherits renderer blue. Graph-reading annotations appear only in solutions. Native diagram labels specify 10 pt and graph ticks 8.5 pt; actual rendering and final-size verification remain for the later capture stage.

examples.derivation: P=(5,3) and Q=(10,6) give k=(6-3)/(10-5)=3/5 GBP per AUD, so p=(3/5)d. Forward reading at d=8 gives p=4.8; reverse reading at p=3 gives d=5. For d=45, p=27. For p=20, d=100/3=33.333..., rounded to 33.33 AUD. Both solution tracing paths meet the plotted line at the correct coordinates.

The labelled point gives k=36/8=4.5 litres per gallon, hence L=4.5G. At L=25, G=25/4.5=50/9=5.555..., consistent with the graphical estimate of 5.6 gallons. The solution trace intersects the line at (50/9,25). The explanation correctly distinguishes graph-reading precision from the exact result within the model.

Graph A is straight and passes through (0,0), satisfying the direct variation origin test. Graph B is straight with vertical intercept 30 mm, so zero attached mass corresponds to non-zero spring length and the relationship is not directly proportional. The solution annotations identify the correct intercepts.
